parameters.name: terrain_cell_mm
parameters.basis: authored: the heightfield sample spacing; the terrain record refuses a cell that does not divide the 128 m tile.

parameters.name: terrain_relief_mm
parameters.basis: authored: the largest elevation range a tile's terrain may span; a bound on grading, not a landform.

parameters.name: city_extent_x_mm
parameters.basis: authored: the bounded work one generation covers, from its south-west corner at the frame origin, along x, east. It is a whole number of 128000 mm tiles, because the terrain stage covers a city with whole patches; the districts stage refuses an extent that ends mid-tile. This stage version divides the extent into one district.

parameters.name: city_extent_y_mm
parameters.basis: authored: the bounded work one generation covers, from its south-west corner at the frame origin, along y, north. It is a whole number of 128000 mm tiles, because the terrain stage covers a city with whole patches; the districts stage refuses an extent that ends mid-tile. This stage version divides the extent into one district.

parameters.name: driving_side
parameters.basis: authored: the side of the carriageway traffic keeps to is a convention a world states, so nothing chooses it: it is required.

parameters.name: block_length_mm
parameters.basis: authored, awaiting admitted statistics: the spacing of cross streets along a street, a planning choice and not a quoted standard. The range stands until an admitted street network statistic replaces it, with no change to this parameter's shape.

parameters.name: block_depth_mm
parameters.basis: authored, awaiting admitted statistics: the spacing of the parallel streets across a street, the partner of block_length_mm. The range stands until an admitted street network statistic replaces it, with no change to this parameter's shape.

parameters.name: lane_width_mm
parameters.basis: authored: about 9 to 12 feet; lane width is discussed in NACTO Urban Street Design Guide (Island Press, 2013), Street Design Elements, Lane Width, which was not re-read in this build and is not quoted.

parameters.name: camber_millionths
parameters.basis: authored: a carriageway cross-fall of 1 to 4 percent from crown to kerb line, for drainage; not quoted from a standard.

parameters.name: crossing_width_mm
parameters.basis: authored: the band a crossing marks along the street; crosswalks are discussed in NACTO Urban Street Design Guide (Island Press, 2013), Street Design Elements, Crosswalks and Crossings, which was not re-read in this build and is not quoted.

parameters.name: speed_limit_mm_s
parameters.basis: authored: 15 to 50 km/h, floored to millimetres per second, a range for inhabited streets; the traffic lane owns the rules that read it.

parameters.name: kerb_height_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': 'Kerb 100 to 180 mm'.

parameters.name: kerb_width_mm
parameters.basis: authored: the width of the kerb top; kerb units of this order are what the kerb-stone texture set depicts.

parameters.name: gutter_width_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': names a gutter; its width is authored, and 0 is a street with no separate gutter strip.

parameters.name: footway_width_mm
parameters.basis: authored: kerb to frontage line; sidewalk zones are discussed in NACTO Urban Street Design Guide (Island Press, 2013), Street Design Elements, Sidewalks, which was not re-read in this build and is not quoted.

parameters.name: footway_crossfall_millionths
parameters.basis: authored: a 1 to 2.5 percent rise from kerb to frontage, so a footway drains to the gutter.

parameters.name: corner_radius_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': names corner radii; the range is authored, with small radii for slow urban turns as discussed in NACTO Urban Street Design Guide (Island Press, 2013), Street Design Elements, Corner Radii, not re-read in this build.

parameters.name: lot_frontage_mm
parameters.basis: authored: the frontage a subdivision aims for, from a narrow shopfront lot to a wide one.

parameters.name: lot_depth_mm
parameters.basis: authored: the depth a subdivision aims for behind the frontage line.

parameters.name: memory_precinct_lots
parameters.basis: authored: how many lots a district reserves as memory precincts, so nothing is ever cut out of a block later (graft 7).

parameters.name: front_setback_mm
parameters.basis: authored: the distance a building stands back from the frontage line; 0 builds to the line.

parameters.name: typology
parameters.basis: authored: the typology catalog's keys, exactly.

parameters.name: era
parameters.basis: authored: the era catalog's keys, exactly.

parameters.name: storeys
parameters.basis: authored: storeys above grade, ground storey included; a typology narrows it.

parameters.name: ground_storey_height_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': 'Ground band 0 to 4.0-6.0 m'.

parameters.name: upper_storey_height_mm
parameters.basis: authored: floor to floor above the ground storey; an era narrows it.

parameters.name: setback_depth_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': names setbacks; the depth range is authored.

parameters.name: setback_top_storeys
parameters.basis: authored: how many top storeys step back; 0 is no setback.

parameters.name: roof_family
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': 'Roof families'; the roof-family catalog's keys, exactly.

parameters.name: roof_rise_mm
parameters.basis: authored: a ridge's height above the wall top; 0 for a flat roof.

parameters.name: parapet_height_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': names parapets; the height range is authored.

parameters.name: light_well_count
parameters.basis: authored: light wells per tier.

parameters.name: rooftop_plant_count
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': names rooftop plant; the count range is authored.

parameters.name: rooftop_tank_count
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': names tanks; the count range is authored.

parameters.name: bay_pitch_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': '2.4 to 3.5 m on centre as frontage / round(frontage / target)'.

parameters.name: opening_width_mm
parameters.basis: authored: a window's width; the record refuses one wider than its bay.

parameters.name: opening_height_mm
parameters.basis: authored: a window's height; an era narrows it.

parameters.name: sill_height_mm
parameters.basis: authored: a window's sill above its storey's floor.

parameters.name: reveal_depth_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': 'Recessed openings, 120 to 250 mm reveal'.

parameters.name: sill_projection_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': names a sill projection; its range is authored.

parameters.name: sill_thickness_mm
parameters.basis: authored: the projecting sill's own height; 0 is no projecting sill.

parameters.name: head_treatment
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': names a head treatment; the four labels are authored, and the geometry is always the explicit rise, band and projection.

parameters.name: head_rise_mm
parameters.basis: authored: a segmental arch's rise over the opening; 0 is a flat head.

parameters.name: head_band_mm
parameters.basis: authored: the height of a lintel or hood above the opening.

parameters.name: head_projection_mm
parameters.basis: authored: how far a lintel or hood stands proud of the face.

parameters.name: string_course_height_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': 'string courses 60 to 200 mm'.

parameters.name: string_course_projection_mm
parameters.basis: authored: how far a string course stands proud; 0 is no string course.

parameters.name: cornice_height_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': 'cornice 400 to 900 mm'.

parameters.name: cornice_projection_mm
parameters.basis: authored: how far a cornice oversails; 0 is no cornice.

parameters.name: stall_riser_height_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': names the stall riser; its height range is authored.

parameters.name: transom_height_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': names the transom; its height range is authored, and 0 is none.

parameters.name: fascia_height_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': names the fascia; its height range is authored.

parameters.name: awning_projection_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': names the awning; its reach is authored, and 0 is none.

parameters.name: awning_valance_mm
parameters.basis: authored: the depth of an awning's front drop.

parameters.name: entrance_recess_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': names a recessed entrance; its depth is authored.

parameters.name: threshold_height_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': names the threshold; its step above the footway is authored.

parameters.name: wall_material
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': surface_material; the options are the material catalog's keys that dress a wall, exactly.

parameters.name: repeat_size_millionths
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': 'per-instance UV scale'; within a quarter of a set's baked size, so a brick stays brick-sized.

parameters.name: soiling_gradient_millionths
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': 'soiling gradient'.

parameters.name: base_weathering_millionths
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': 'base weathering'.

parameters.name: reveal_darkening_millionths
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': 'reveal darkening'.

parameters.name: tree_species
parameters.basis: derived: the tree-species catalog's keys, exactly, which come from the NYC 2015 Street Tree Census retained under assets/catalogs/sources.

parameters.name: tree_spacing_mm
parameters.basis: authored: the spacing of street trees along a kerb.

parameters.name: lamp_spacing_mm
parameters.basis: authored: the spacing of street lamps along a kerb; not a lighting calculation.

parameters.name: furniture_kerb_offset_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': 'street furniture at kerb offsets'; the range is authored.

parameters.name: exclusion_clearance_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': 'exclusion zones'; the clearance range is authored.

parameters.name: vitrine_depth_mm
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': 'a lit vitrine behind the glass', 0.6 to 1.5 m deep.

parameters.name: fitout
parameters.basis: authored: the fitout catalog's keys, exactly.

parameters.name: vitrine_light_level_millionths
parameters.basis: target architecture 2026-09-15, table 'Why it clears the bar': the vitrine is lit; the level is relative to the brightest the renderer shows.

parameters.name: ground_floor_use
parameters.basis: authored: the use-class catalog's keys, exactly, which the living society lane maps to roles.

parameters.name: upper_floor_use
parameters.basis: authored: the use-class catalog's keys, exactly.

parameters.name: units_per_storey
parameters.basis: authored: how many premises share one storey.

navigation.reason: The ground of a block that no lot covers is drawn level at its grade and stood on.

A crossing draws its own band across the carriageway, surface role crossing with its own material and kerb upstand, rather than only marking the carriageway, so its drawn horizontal surface is where a person crossing stands.
Its kerb top and footway, along its straight pieces and round the corner it owns, are drawn horizontal surfaces a person stands on; its kerb face is a step, not support.
A region of the parameter cascade; it draws nothing.
The floor of a recessed entrance, from the face line to the door, is drawn and stood on.

A facade draws walls, not ground. Every part it puts beyond its building's base ring stands at least the capsule height above the building's base (facade_clearance), so it obstructs no standing capsule, and the building's base ring obstructs for the rest.
Its panels are set into the building within its base ring, and its awning stands at least the capsule height above the base (facade_clearance).
Its carriageway fill inside the kerb arcs is drawn and may be stood on.
A relation stating how a segment enters its junction; it draws nothing.
A path on its segment's carriageway, which the segment draws and supports.
A path across its junction's fill, which the junction draws and supports.
The ground under a building's base ring is neither drawn nor stood on, and a standing capsule keeps its radius clear of that ring.
A lot outside its building is drawn level at its grade and stood on.
A space on a carriageway or a footway, whose surface that carriageway or footway draws; its bay lines are markings.
An occupancy of its building; it draws nothing of its own.
Paint on a surface another record draws and supports.
It stands on a roof, and no roof supports a person in this version.
A relation naming the furniture that draws its heads; it draws nothing.
A name over its segments, which draw.

Lamps, benches, bins, stands and poles stand on the footway. A standing capsule keeps its radius clear of every part whose bottom is below the capsule height; a lamp's arm or a signal's head above it obstructs nobody.
A point of the street network; its junction or its segments' ends draw.
Its carriageway and gutters are drawn between its kerb lines and may be stood on.
Its pit is drawn ground a person may stand on and its trunk obstructs as a low part; its canopy stands at least the capsule height above every support surface it overhangs (canopy_clearance).
A dressing a drawn surface cites; it draws nothing.
The heightfield is drawn and stood on wherever no other record's drawn ground or covered region lies over it.
The inputs of one bake, not a subject; it draws nothing.
A lit volume inside its building, behind glazing.
